title: Segregation of duties in finance
context: At LearnTech, Finance sets suppliers up and pays them in its finance systems, and plans the spend in Workday Adaptive Planning, this lab's product, which is named here only for context. LedgerSim is a brand-neutral simulator that shows the same governance information: users and roles, approval workflows, the vendor master and payments. All amounts are in EUR. All finance data is synthetic.
atWork: At work, a junior analyst checks the finance system behind a supplier decision: who can set up a vendor and pay it alone, whether bank-detail changes were verified, and whether payments kept to their approvers' limits.
owner: SOC-DEC records the Group's onboarding decision on a supplier. Once a supplier is decided, Procurement sets it up in the finance system and Accounts payable pay it, so the decision only holds if nobody can set up a supplier and pay it alone. Before SOC-DEC is filed, check LearnTech's finance system in LedgerSim, as of today: who can both create vendors and approve payments, and what stands behind each of them; vendor bank-detail changes made without the call-back the workflow asks for, and whether anything was paid after them; and payments approved above the approver's limit. Capture what you find, so the file can rely on it without anyone opening the console.
rules: Document toxic combinations (segregation-of-duties conflicts) and block them in the role design. LedgerSim's SoD matrix is Finance's list of them: two roles marked No may not be held by one account.

Exceptions require a documented risk assessment, compensating controls, a named owner, an expiry date (maximum 12 months) and approval per the delegated authority in the GRC Charter Section 6.1. An SoD exception allows the one conflict, for the one account it names, until it expires; it allows nothing else.
Shared and generic accounts are prohibited, except break-glass accounts that are registered, sealed and monitored.
Ref-Actions U3 and U5 (Access Reviews › Track Remediation)
U3, shared/generic account not registered: register as break-glass or disable. U5, segregation-of-duties conflict: remove one of the two roles. Both: the system owner, within 5 working days.

All staff must report suspected incidents immediately via the service desk or security hotline. A payment made to bank details changed without the call-back may have gone to someone posing as the supplier: that is a suspected incident.

views.title: Users & roles
views.sub: Finance-system accounts and their roles. A person's account carries their name; a shared account carries a team's. Approval limit is the largest payment the account may approve.

views.title: SoD matrix
views.sub: Segregation-of-duties matrix used by Finance: may one account hold both roles?

views.title: SoD exceptions
views.sub: Each lets one account hold Vendor maintainer and AP approver together, with a compensating control, until it expires.
rows: Finance Controller reviews the vendor master change log each month
Finance Controller reviews the vendor master change log each month
Finance Controller reviews every vendor master change each week and signs the log
AP team lead reviews the account's payments each month

views.title: Approval workflows
views.sub: The approval rules Finance has set in the system.
rows: Approver's limit must be ≥ payment amount
Independent call-back to a known number + second approver

views.title: Vendor master
views.sub: Vendor master change log, last 90 days. Call-back verified: whether someone called the vendor back on a number already on file before the change was approved.

views.title: Payments
views.sub: Supplier payments, last 60 days, in EUR. Approver limit is the approving account's limit.

parts.title: Who can set up a vendor and pay it
parts.ask: Find every active account that can both create or change vendors and approve payments, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Users & roles. Roles says what each role does, and the SoD matrix which pairs Finance does not allow. Use two filters together. Press Capture evidence, then choose the capture here.

parts.title: What is done about each one?
parts.ask: For each account you captured, choose what is done about it.
parts.where: SoD exceptions lists the exceptions on record and when each expires; the console's date is in the dark bar above the table. Users & roles gives each account's name. BKB-POL-006 Sections 3.1 and 8 and Ref-Actions are in The rules you apply.
options: U5: remove one of the two roles
U3: register as break-glass or disable

parts.title: Bank-detail changes without a call-back
parts.ask: Find every bank-detail change made without the call-back the workflow asks for, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Vendor master. Approval workflows says what a bank-detail change needs. Use two filters together.

parts.title: Was anything paid after the change?
parts.ask: For each change you captured, decide what is done now.
parts.where: Vendor master gives each change's vendor and date. Payments lists each payment's vendor and date. BKB-POL-014 Section 3.1 is in The rules you apply.
options: Paid since: report a suspected incident now
Nothing paid since: block payments until verified

parts.title: Payments above the approver's limit
parts.ask: Find every payment approved above its approver's limit, and capture exactly those.
parts.where: Payments gives each payment's amount and its approver's limit. Approval workflows says what a supplier payment needs.
